look_here_first: Do not start with pink color. Inspect ONE flower head from the SIDE with a scale. Fleischmannia has a short 4–5 mm involucre and comparatively few phyllary ranks; fragrant mistflower (Chromolaena odorata) has a more cylindrical ~8–10 mm head with many overlapping phyllary rows. Next check Fleischmannia's lax/sprawling herbaceous stems and opposite coarsely toothed triangular-to-heart-shaped leaves. Against blue mistflower (Conoclinium coelestinum), also compare florets per head and flat/slightly convex vs conic receptacle if a dissection is possible.

morphology.habit: Perennial 30–120(–200) cm, lax, sprawling or scandent/leaning on neighbors, much branched.
morphology.leaves: Opposite; petioles (0.5–)1–3.5(–4) cm; triangular-deltate 2–5(–7) × 1.5–3.5(–5) cm; base often truncate to cordate, margins coarsely serrate to crenate-serrate.
morphology.heads: Small discoid heads in terminal corymbiform clusters; FNA 4–5 mm involucres, outer phyllaries lanceolate and inner narrowly oblong-lanceolate.
morphology.florets: Florets fewer (often ~13–25 per head in regional treatments) than Conoclinium (35–70+); pink-purple/whitish with pink or lilac lobes.
morphology.receptacle: Flat or slightly convex in Fleischmannia; Conoclinium genus characterized by conspicuously conic receptacle (requires dissection/closeup).
morphology.carpopodium: FNA describes stopper-shaped, sharply separated carpopodium in Fleischmannia, compared with less well developed carpopodium in Ageratina; use only with careful microscope view.
morphology.fruit: FNA cypselae 1.8–2.8 mm, usually sparsely strigoso-hirtellous, sometimes glabrate. Variation makes pubescence alone insufficient.

separators: Fleischmannia: lax climbing/sprawling stems; Conoclinium often more erect/colonial
Fleischmannia fewer florets per head (commonly 13–25) vs Conoclinium typically 35–70+
Fleischmannia receptacle nearly flat vs conic in Conoclinium
Fleischmannia heads often pinkish; color alone unreliable
Fleischmannia usually thin/lax HERBACEOUS stems vs A. havanensis woody persistent shrub framework
Fleischmannia carpopodium more strongly differentiated and stopper-shaped; microscopical confirmation
A. havanensis often denser white heads; cannot ID from color alone
Inspect the SIDE of one unopened-to-flowering capitulum: Fleischmannia involucre 4–5 mm, Chromolaena odorata typically cylindrical 8–10 mm.
Fleischmannia heads have relatively few phyllary ranks; Chromolaena has conspicuously numerous overlapping/imbricate phyllary series.
Fleischmannia stems are lax, sprawling or weakly climbing HERBACEOUS growth; Chromolaena more robust and shrub-like, but this is supporting only.
Both can bear opposite coarsely toothed, three-veined-looking leaves and pinkish flower heads: neither color nor leaf venation alone separates them.

separators: White snakeroot commonly has broader triangular opposite toothed leaves and white head clusters, but flower color overlaps.
When sterile or atypical, inspect capitulum phyllaries and mature fruit; avoid an identification based on white versus pink alone.
